samuel1.25.p1.b1.text: When Samuel died, all Israel gathered to mourn for him; and they buried him at his home in Ramah.

samuel1.25.p1.b2.text: Then David set out and went down to the Wilderness of Paran.

samuel1.25.p2.b1.text: Now there was a man in Maon…He was a very wealthy man with a thousand goats and three thousand sheep, which he was shearing in Carmel.

samuel1.25.p2.b2.text: His name was Nabal, and his wife’s name was Abigail. She was an intelligent and beautiful woman, but her husband, a Calebite, was harsh and evil in his dealings.

samuel1.25.p2.b3.text: and say to him, ‘Long life to you, and peace to you and your house and to all that belongs to you.

samuel1.25.p2.b4.text: So David sent ten young men…Please give whatever you can afford to your servants and to your son David.

samuel1.25.p3.b1.text: When David’s young men arrived, they relayed all these words to Nabal on behalf of David. Then they waited.

samuel1.25.p3.b2.text: Who is David? Who is this son of Jesse? Many servants these days are breaking away from their masters. Why should I take my bread and water…and give them to these men whose origin I do not know?

samuel1.25.p3.b4.text: about four hundred men followed David, while two hundred stayed with the supplies.

samuel1.25.p4.b1.text: Meanwhile, one of Nabal’s young men informed Nabal’s wife Abigail…

samuel1.25.p4.b2.text: Look, David sent messengers from the wilderness to greet our master, but he scolded them.

samuel1.25.p4.b3.text: Yet these men were very good to us…They were a wall around us, both day and night, the whole time we were herding our sheep near them.

samuel1.25.p4.b4.text: Now consider carefully what you must do…For he is such a scoundrel that nobody can speak to him!

samuel1.25.p5.b1.text: Then Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves of bread, two skins of wine, five butchered sheep, five seahs of roasted grain, a hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs. She loaded them on donkeys

samuel1.25.p5.b2.text: Go ahead of me. I will be right behind you.

samuel1.25.p5.b3.text: But she did not tell her husband Nabal.

samuel1.25.p5.b4.text: As Abigail came riding her donkey into a mountain ravine, she saw David and his men coming down toward her, and she met them.

samuel1.25.p6.b1.text: In vain I have protected all that belonged to this man in the wilderness…he has paid me back evil for good.

samuel1.25.p6.b2.text: When Abigail saw David, she quickly got off the donkey, fell facedown, and bowed before him. She fell at his feet…

samuel1.25.p6.b3.text: My lord, may the blame be on me alone, but please let your servant speak to you; hear the words of your servant.

samuel1.25.p7.b1.text: My lord should pay no attention to this scoundrel Nabal, for he lives up to his name: His name means Fool, and folly accompanies him.

samuel1.25.p7.b2.text: Now, my lord…the LORD has held you back from coming to bloodshed and avenging yourself with your own hand.

samuel1.25.p7.b3.text: Now let this gift your servant has brought to my lord be given to the young men who follow you.

samuel1.25.p7.b4.text: the LORD will surely make a lasting dynasty for my lord, because he fights the LORD’s battles.

samuel1.25.p8.b1.text: And should someone pursue you and seek your life, then the life of my lord will be bound securely by the LORD your God in the bundle of the living.

samuel1.25.p8.b2.text: But He shall fling away the lives of your enemies like stones from a sling.

samuel1.25.p8.b3.text: then my lord will have no remorse or guilt of conscience over needless bloodshed and revenge.

samuel1.25.p8.b4.text: And when the LORD has dealt well with my lord, may you remember your maidservant.

samuel1.25.p9.b1.text: Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who sent you to meet me this day!

samuel1.25.p9.b2.text: Blessed is your discernment, and blessed are you, because today you kept me from bloodshed and from avenging myself by my own hand.

samuel1.25.p9.b3.text: Go home in peace. See, I have heeded your voice and granted your request.

samuel1.25.p10.b1.text: When Abigail returned to Nabal, there he was in the house, holding a feast fit for a king, in high spirits and very drunk. So she told him nothing…

samuel1.25.p10.b2.text: In the morning when Nabal was sober, his wife told him about these events…

samuel1.25.p10.b3.text: and his heart failed within him and he became like a stone.

samuel1.25.p10.b4.text: About ten days later, the LORD struck Nabal dead.

samuel1.25.p11.b1.text: Blessed be the LORD, who has upheld my cause against the reproach of Nabal and has restrained His servant from evil…

samuel1.25.p11.b2.text: David has sent us to take you as his wife.

samuel1.25.p11.b3.text: Here is your maidservant, ready to serve and to wash the feet of my lord’s servants.

samuel1.25.p11.b4.text: So Abigail hurried and got on a donkey, and attended by five of her maidens, she followed David’s messengers and became his wife.

samuel1.25.p11.b5.text: But Saul had given his daughter Michal, David’s wife, to Palti son of Laish…
